title: Follow the Mean: Reference-Guided Flow Matching
claim: Steering a frozen generative model with a reference set shifts its flow toward the references, changing the output without retraining or rewards.
layout: Gallery strip on top, single flow diagram below; two trajectories diverge from noise, left-to-right
description: The top row shows four labeled before/after image pairs: Style change, Attribute change, Anatomy fix, and Compositionality. Each pair has a gray-bordered baseline image and a pink-bordered guided image. Below is a prompt box reading 'Realistic image of an elephant in a jungle'. The main diagram starts at a Gaussian noise bump labeled p0 (noise) on the left. A gray curve goes to the gray-bordered 'Output', a realistic gray elephant in a jungle. A pink curve branches to the 'Reference-guided output (Ours)', a pink elephant in a jungle. At the branch point, a dashed gray arrow marks the model flow. A thick pink arrow marks the reference-guided flow. Thinner pink arrows point down to four pink elephant reference images, with the caption 'Reference set of pink elephant images (chosen at inference time)'. A pink gradient panel highlights the proposed method, and the eye goes first to the elephants.
caption: Reference-guided flow matching steers a frozen model with examples. A noisy state is matched against a reference set R, which shifts the endpoint mean away from the pretrained prediction, so the flow takes on characteristics of the references without a classifier or reward.
abstract: Existing approaches to controllable generation typically rely on fine-tuning, auxiliary networks, or test-time search. We show that flow matching admits a different control interface: adaptation through examples. For deterministic interpolants, the velocity field is solely governed by a conditional endpoint mean, so shifting this mean shifts the flow itself, and a pretrained model can be steered simply by changing the reference set it follows. We instantiate this idea in two forms. Reference-Mean Guidance is training-free. It computes a closed-form correction to the endpoint mean from a reference bank and applies it to a frozen FLUX.2-klein (4B) model, controlling color, identity, style, and structure while the prompt, seed, and weights stay fixed. Semi-Parametric Guidance builds the same principle into a trained model through an explicit mean anchor and a learned residual refiner, matching the quality of an unconditional DiT-B/4 on AFHQv2 while allowing the reference set to be swapped at inference time. Together, these results point to a broader direction: generative models that adapt through data rather than parameter updates.
